tour.name: Fátima, Batalha, Nazaré & Óbidos Private Day Trip from Lisbon
tour.subtitle: Portugal's heartland in one private day with a licensed guide and vehicle: the sanctuary of Fátima, the Gothic monastery of Batalha, the giant waves and fishing traditions of Nazaré, and the walled medieval village of Óbidos with a glass of ginjinha in a chocolate cup.

tour.overview:
North of Lisbon, central Portugal combines faith, history and the sea. At Fátima, three shepherd children reported apparitions of the Virgin Mary in 1917, and millions of pilgrims now visit each year. Batalha's monastery, built to celebrate a victory over Castile in 1385, is a masterpiece of Gothic architecture and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Nazaré is a fishing town whose canyon produces some of the largest surfed waves in the world, and Óbidos is a medieval village enclosed by walls, given as a wedding gift by kings to their queens.

This private day links them all with a licensed guide and a vehicle.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 10 hours
• Start and end: your hotel in Lisbon
• Type: private tour with licensed guide, vehicle and driver
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: easy

WHAT YOU SEE
• Fátima.
• Batalha Monastery.
• Nazaré.
• Óbidos.

WHY THIS WORKS
These four places are spread across the region; a private vehicle makes it possible in one day at a relaxed pace.

WHO IT SUITS
Families, couples, pilgrims and photographers.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
For Alcobaça and Tomar, ask us for a variation of this tour.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
Giant waves at Nazaré appear mainly from October to March during big swells. Fátima is busiest on the 12th and 13th of May and October.

days.name: Fátima, Batalha, Nazaré and Óbidos
days.description:
What to expect: the pilgrimage sanctuary, a Gothic monastery, a fishing town and a medieval village, with a licensed guide and private vehicle.

Your guide and driver collect you at about 8:30 and drive north, about 1 hour 30 minutes, to Fátima. In the vast sanctuary, you see the Chapel of the Apparitions, the basilica where the three shepherd children are buried, and the modern Basilica of the Holy Trinity.

At Batalha, you visit the monastery, with its soaring nave, the Founder's Chapel with the tombs of King João I and Philippa of Lancaster, the royal cloister carved in Manueline lace, and the roofless Unfinished Chapels.

After lunch of grilled fish in Nazaré (not included), you take the funicular up to the Sítio, a clifftop above the town, and look out to the fort where giant waves of up to 20 metres or more break in winter. Women in the traditional seven petticoats sell dried fish by the beach. You end in Óbidos, walking along its walls and its lane of white houses trimmed in blue and yellow, and taste ginjinha, a cherry liqueur, served in a chocolate cup.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
08:30 – Pick-up in Lisbon.
10:00 – Fátima.
11:30 – Batalha Monastery.
13:00 – Lunch in Nazaré.
14:30 – Sítio and the fort.
16:00 – Óbidos.
18:30 – Back in Lisbon.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Alcobaça Monastery can replace Batalha.
• In winter, your guide checks the wave forecast for Nazaré.

INCLUDED: private vehicle and driver, licensed guide, monastery ticket, ginjinha, bottled water, hotel pick-up and drop-off.
NOT INCLUDED: lunch, tips.

Overnight: none.
Meals: tasting.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: Will we see the giant waves?
faq.answer: Only during big swells, mainly from October to March; your guide checks the forecast.

faq.question: Is lunch included?
faq.answer: No. Nazaré has excellent fish restaurants.

faq.question: Can we attend Mass in Fátima?
faq.answer: Yes. Services are held regularly; tell us and we will plan around them.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes. Child seats are provided free of charge on request.

faq.question: Is it suitable for people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: Largely. The walls of Óbidos are narrow with no railings; the village itself is accessible.

faq.question: Can we add Alcobaça or Tomar?
Is it a long day?
faq.answer: About 10 hours, with roughly 4 hours of driving.

faq.question: Will we be taken to shops?
faq.answer: No. There are no commission stops.

faq.question: What should we wear?
faq.answer: Comfortable shoes, layers and modest dress for Fátima.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
faq.answer: All year. Winter for the big waves; spring and autumn for mild weather.

faq.question: Should we tip?
faq.answer: Tipping is not obligatory in Portugal, but rounding up or leaving 5 to 10 percent for a guide or driver you were happy with is appreciated.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 24 hours before the tour. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
